price_stale_note: PPG.AX has been suspended from ASX quotation since 1 September 2025 (Listing Rule 17.5, failure to lodge the FY2025 annual report) and the group entered voluntary administration on 23 October 2025. Yahoo Finance no longer serves the symbol at all ('No data found, symbol may be delisted', checked 2026-11-15), so there is no quote to fetch. current_price is DERIVED, not quoted: the stockanalysis.com market capitalisation stored in info.json (A$3.27m, fetched 2026-09-22, itself a frozen pre-suspension figure) divided by 181.688m shares on issue. price_as_of is the last ASX session before the suspension took effect; the exact date of the last actual trade was not verified. The figure is a non-transactable artifact retained only because the pipeline requires current_price; upside figures against it are not economically meaningful.
model: Asset / creditor waterfall (insolvent, voluntary administration) - not a going-concern model
model_note: Pro-Pac Packaging is NOT a going concern and NOT a DCF candidate. Routed via the dcf-methods table row 'Distressed, receivership, delisted, cash shell -> asset or creditor waterfall'. Sequence: strategic review (Feb-2025) -> ASX suspension (1-Sep-2025) -> voluntary administration of 23 Australian and 2 NZ entities (23-Oct-2025, McGrathNicol Restructuring) -> Business Sale Agreements (21-Jan-2026) selling the Australian business (excluding Perfection Packaging, wound down) and the NZ business to KnoxCorp subsidiaries. The operating assets have left the listed entity, so there is no forward cash flow to project. UNLIKE the CBD.NZ precedent, no sale price and no creditor-tier dollar amounts have been disclosed for PPG. This valuation therefore rests PRIMARILY on the administrators' own public statement that sale proceeds will not be sufficient to provide any return to shareholders, and only secondarily on the last reported balance sheet (31-Dec-2024). The waterfall below is a structural ordering of claims with last-reported book figures for context; it is not an arithmetic reconstruction of the actual distribution, and undisclosed lines are left null rather than invented.

inputs.shares_outstanding_note: 181.688m ordinary shares on issue (FY2024 annual report and H1 FY2025), unchanged since the FY2023 rights issue. No dilutive adjustment is relevant: equity ranks last and receives nothing.
inputs.net_debt_note: Not meaningful as a DCF input. Last reported net debt was A$41.1m at 31-Dec-2024 (interest-bearing liabilities less cash, pre-AASB 16, excluding A$7.3m of net government-grant proceeds), up from A$27.8m at 30-Jun-2024 and A$15.0m at 30-Jun-2023. That figure is 11 months stale at the administration date and precedes the further A$3m secured Bennamon facility of Aug-2025. Balances at appointment are undisclosed.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Deliberately omitted. No repeatable free cash flow exists: reported FCF was negative in FY2022 (-A$10.7m), FY2023 (-A$10.7m), FY2024 (-A$7.2m) and H1 FY2025 (-A$8.3m), and the operating businesses have since been sold out of the listed entity.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2024 (last audited year), A$ millions, for historical disclosure only.
inputs.sbc_source: Metrics.csv StockBasedComp, FY2024 (-A$0.471m, a net reversal of prior share-based payment expense). Immaterial; no going-concern flows to adjust.
inputs.share_count_basis: Shares on issue, held flat; no projection applies.
inputs.balance_sheet_note: The latest balance sheet that exists. The FY2025 annual report was never lodged (the cause of the suspension) and ASIC relief defers reporting until the end of the administration or 23-Oct-2027. Every book figure here predates the administration by about ten months of further trading losses.
inputs.notes: Model: creditor waterfall, chosen because the entity is insolvent, suspended and has sold its operating businesses out of administration. Not an owner-FCF DCF. First valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF, no memory entry). No sale price or creditor amounts are public; base and bear take the administrators' stated conclusion (nil to shareholders) as the answer. The 3% bull case is a token speculative allowance, not an estimate derived from disclosed numbers. The Bennamon facility amounts (A$13m, then a further A$3m secured in Aug-2025), the ScotPac funding deed and the administrators' statement come from the qualitative analysis (Analysis.json) and the task brief; of these only the A$13m major-shareholder facility was confirmed directly in a filing (H1 FY2025 report).

waterfall.basis: Structural priority ordering. Realisations and creditor balances at appointment are undisclosed; figures shown are last-reported book values for context only and must not be read as the distribution.
waterfall.gross_realisations_note: UNDISCLOSED. Neither the administrators (McGrathNicol) nor the purchaser (KnoxCorp) has published the consideration under the 21-Jan-2026 Business Sale Agreements, and no creditor-tier schedule was available in the sources reviewed. Left null rather than estimated. The sale covered the Australian business (ex-Perfection Packaging) and the NZ business on a going-concern basis. Perfection Packaging was wound down (closure Feb-2026), which realises assets piecemeal and crystallises redundancy and lease-exit costs.
waterfall.administration_costs_note: UNDISCLOSED. Administrators' remuneration, legal costs (including Federal Court and NZ High Court applications), trading-on losses during the administration and wind-down costs rank ahead of all pre-appointment claims. For a 25-entity trans-Tasman administration running from Oct-2025 through at least the Jan-2026 sale these are plausibly in the mid-to-high single-digit millions, but that is an inference, not a disclosed figure, and is used only in the illustrative sensitivity grid.
waterfall.secured_creditors_note: Balances at appointment UNDISCLOSED. Known secured or financing claimants: ANZ (bank overdraft; covenant waiver required at 30-Jun-2024), a debtor finance facility (A$18.1m drawn of a A$30.0m limit at 30-Jun-2024, committed to Dec-2025), a ScotPac funding deed referenced in a Federal Court judgment during the administration, and major shareholder Bennamon Pty Ltd (A$13.0m facility, plus a further A$3.0m secured facility in Aug-2025). Last reported net debt of A$41.1m (31-Dec-2024) is the only quantified anchor and predates the Aug-2025 top-up.
waterfall.priority_employee_creditors_note: UNDISCLOSED. Employee entitlements rank ahead of ordinary unsecured creditors (and ahead of circulating-asset security). Entitlements of transferring staff were presumably assumed by the purchaser in a going-concern sale; those of Perfection Packaging staff made redundant fall on the estate.
waterfall.lease_liabilities_note: A$48.5m of AASB 16 lease liabilities at 30-Jun-2024. Leases for continuing sites were presumably assigned to the purchaser; closed sites generate unsecured lessor claims. Split undisclosed.
waterfall.unsecured_creditors_note: Balance at appointment UNDISCLOSED. Trade and related-party payables were A$37.2m at 30-Jun-2024. A further possible claim is repayment of Modern Manufacturing Initiative grant proceeds (A$7.3m net held, soft-plastics recycling plant never completed); its status is unknown.
waterfall.last_reported_net_assets_note: Book net assets of A$45.6m at 31-Dec-2024 (A$81.1m at 30-Jun-2024, A$135.8m at 30-Jun-2023), after A$22.7m of FY2024 and A$20.7m of H1 FY2025 impairments. This was the entire book cushion beneath all creditors. For equity to receive anything, the combined erosion after that date (Jan-Oct 2025 trading losses, the discount of a distressed sale to book value, Perfection Packaging closure costs, administration costs) would have to total less than A$45.6m. The H1 FY2025 loss alone was A$36.8m in six months.
waterfall.residual_to_ordinary_shareholders_note: NIL in base and bear, taken directly from the administrators' public statement that sale proceeds will not be sufficient to provide any return to shareholders. This is the administrators' disclosed conclusion, not a figure derived here by arithmetic: the inputs needed to derive it are not public.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Not applicable in the conventional sense: no growth rate is selected because nothing is projected. CAGRs are to FY2024, the last audited year. Revenue CAGRs are distorted downward by the 2022 divestment of the Rigid and Source & Sell businesses (FY2019-FY2022 figures include them). EPS and FCF CAGRs are null because the end values are negative (FY2024 EPS -A$0.296, FCF -A$7.2m). Equity was still shrinking faster after the measurement date: A$81.1m at Jun-2024 to A$45.6m at Dec-2024, a 44% fall in six months.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue A$m: FY2019 485.8, FY2020 478.2, FY2021 440.1, FY2022 467.0, FY2023 341.3 (continuing), FY2024 295.2, H1 FY2025 142.9 (-10.1% yoy). Net income A$m: FY2022 -25.9, FY2023 -10.2, FY2024 -53.8, H1 FY2025 -36.8. EBITDA pre-AASB 16: FY2023 1.0, FY2024 -7.6, H1 FY2025 -6.4. SBC is immaterial (FY2024 a -A$0.47m reversal), so owner FCF and reported FCF coincide; both were negative every period from FY2022. Share capital of A$320.5m had been reduced to A$45.6m of net assets by Dec-2024.

base.narrative: The administration concludes as the administrators have said it will. Proceeds of the KnoxCorp sale and the Perfection Packaging wind-down, after administration costs, are absorbed by secured lenders (ANZ, debtor financier, Bennamon), employee priority claims and unsecured creditors. Shareholders receive nothing and the listed entity is eventually liquidated or deregistered.
base.discounting_note: No cash flow stream exists to discount. This is a point-in-time priority waterfall, and its conclusion is the administrators' disclosed statement rather than a computed residual.

bull.narrative: SPECULATIVE, low probability. The administrators' statement proves conservative: realisations (including any deferred consideration, debtor collections or recoveries on the Perfection Packaging assets) exceed expectations and admitted creditor claims come in lower, leaving a small surplus after all creditors. Nothing disclosed supports this; it is included only because final creditor outcomes are not yet published and the statement was made before final adjudication of claims. A A$1.8m residual is a token placeholder, about 4% of the Dec-2024 book net assets, not an estimate derived from data. Bennamon, as both a secured creditor and the roughly 66% shareholder, would take about two-thirds of any such residual.

bear.narrative: Proceeds fall short of secured debt, so unsecured creditors also take a loss. For shareholders the outcome is identical to base: nil. Bear differs from base only in how far up the creditor stack the shortfall reaches.

scenario_narratives.base: Administration completes as stated: creditors absorb all proceeds, nil to equity.
scenario_narratives.bull: Speculative token surplus (A$1.8m, about A$0.01/share) if realisations beat and claims undershoot the administrators' expectation. 3% weight.
scenario_narratives.bear: Shortfall reaches secured or unsecured creditors; nil to equity.

base.note: No projection is modelled. Point-in-time creditor waterfall; the operating businesses were sold out of the listed entity in Jan-2026.

bull.note: No projection is modelled. Point-in-time creditor waterfall; the operating businesses were sold out of the listed entity in Jan-2026.

bear.note: No projection is modelled. Point-in-time creditor waterfall; the operating businesses were sold out of the listed entity in Jan-2026.

base.methodology: Priority waterfall with undisclosed line amounts. Residual to equity is NIL per the administrators' public statement that sale proceeds will not provide any return to shareholders.

bull.methodology: Token speculative surplus of A$1.8m over 181.688m shares. A placeholder for the tail in which the final creditor outcome is better than the administrators indicated; not derived from any disclosed figure.

bear.methodology: Shortfall extends into the creditor stack. Total loss for ordinary equity.

entry_price.rationale: There is no price at which PPG.AX equity is investable. The shares are suspended and cannot be bought or sold on market, the operating businesses have been sold, and the administrators have stated shareholders will receive no return. The IRR entry-price formula needs interim cash flows and a terminal value and is undefined here. Entry price A$0.00 means 'uninvestable', not 'buy at zero'.

sensitivity.description: A WACC / terminal-growth grid is meaningless here. Because realisations and claims are undisclosed, this grid is ILLUSTRATIVE ONLY: it starts from the one disclosed anchor, book net assets of A$45.6m at 31-Dec-2024, and shows the per-share residual after (rows) erosion of those net assets between Dec-2024 and realisation (trading losses, distressed-sale discount to book, closure costs) and (columns) administration costs.
sensitivity.matrix_read_note: Cell = max(0, 45.6 - erosion - administration costs) / 181.688. The administrators' statement implies the true operating point is in the zero region, i.e. erosion plus costs of at least A$45.6m. For scale: the H1 FY2025 loss was A$36.8m in six months, and ten further months of trading plus a distressed sale followed. The positive cells require the business to have lost little value after Dec-2024, which the subsequent insolvency contradicts.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Not the house 15/50/35, which presumes a going concern with symmetric operating scenarios. Base and bear (97% combined) both give nil to equity and differ only in creditor recoveries; the 60/37 split between them is immaterial to the equity value. The combined 97% reflects that the party running the process and holding the actual numbers has said publicly that shareholders get nothing. Bull at 3% is a judgmental allowance for that statement proving conservative once claims are finally adjudicated; it is not calibrated to data and could reasonably be set to zero.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street bases coincide (no SBC adjustment applies to a waterfall); the band is collapsed.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.checks_replaced: model is asset_waterfall: no multiples rule applies; the historical table is reported for context only
sanity_check.fix_applied: none required - creditor waterfall used in place of a growth DCF

valuation_philosophy.why_dcf_was_rejected: A DCF needs a repeatable forward cash flow stream and a terminal value. Pro-Pac has neither. Free cash flow was negative in every period from FY2022, EBITDA before leases turned negative in FY2024, the group entered voluntary administration in October 2025, and its Australian and New Zealand operating businesses were sold to KnoxCorp in January 2026. Whatever cash those businesses generate now belongs to the purchaser. Projecting growth and margins for the listed entity would model a business it no longer owns.
valuation_philosophy.what_is_and_is_not_known: Known: the sequence of events; the administrators' statement that shareholders will receive no return; the 31-Dec-2024 balance sheet (net assets A$45.6m, net debt A$41.1m); the identity of the main secured claimants. Not known: the sale price; administration costs; secured, priority and unsecured creditor balances at appointment; creditor recovery rates; whether a DOCA or liquidation followed the sale; the fate of the A$7.3m government grant. The nil conclusion rests on the first group, chiefly the administrators' statement. It does not depend on reconstructing the second.
valuation_philosophy.conclusion: Ordinary equity in Pro-Pac Packaging (PPG.AX) should be treated as worthless. The administrators have said the business sale will not return anything to shareholders, the shares cannot be traded, and the last balance sheet shows a book cushion that was being consumed at well over A$30m per half-year before the insolvency. The probability-weighted value of about A$0.0003 per share comes entirely from a 3% speculative allowance and is not a basis for holding or buying the stock.
key_risks_to_valuation: The administrators' statement is taken at face value; no creditor report was available to verify it.
Sale consideration and all creditor balances are undisclosed, so the size of the shortfall, and hence how remote the bull case is, cannot be measured.
current_price is derived from a stale market capitalisation, not a quote.
